root_cause: Production deploy 6ab58c611214c700089b7a93 was ready on exact main 4aac008ef0872ab902e5888547bafc991c9eb259 and route checks passed, but the pricing ready-v3 marker never appeared. prijzen.html still referenced pricing-interactions-rescue-v1.js with fixed cache key v=20260924-0750 while the asset had changed later; Git history shows a later asset change at f13e524d and the current asset Git blob is f7d85cb0d7ba7ff8c055895677a906066e702d83. New HTML could therefore load a stale cached rescue runtime. The first cache-identity recovery updated source HTML and snapshot proof but missed tools/site-shell/pricing-build-integrity.mjs, which still hard-coded v=20260924-0750 and could restore that stale runtime reference during the build. Skill Projection exposed the drift because the historical replay read the build transform and failed.
prevention_rule: Static runtime cache identity must be one invariant across source HTML, every build/transform/restoration path, and production content proof. A regression must derive the exact asset Git blob identity from file bytes and assert the same key in all three surfaces. Never patch only source HTML when a build integrity layer can re-inject runtime tags.

provider_evidence.failed_step: Verify pricing interactions and English route in production

invariants: pricing rescue runtime query key equals the current JS Git blob SHA prefix
production snapshot validates the exact same rescue runtime cache key
pricing ready-v3 remains product-specific runtime readiness authority
pricing source HTML build integrity transform and production snapshot share the same content-addressed rescue runtime key

failed_approaches: Updating the source HTML and Production Source Snapshot cache key without updating pricing-build-integrity.mjs, allowing the build transform to re-inject the stale timestamp key.
Using an over-escaped dynamic RegExp in the cache-identity regression, causing a false-negative Skill Projection failure.
